title: How Do You Automate Client Account Management at Agencies?
summary: See how agencies and consultancies automate client account management, approvals, and deliverables at scale.
body_markdown:
Automating client accounts at agencies and consultancies means structuring each client's flow (onboarding, deliverable approval, billing) in a single environment, with automations that fire as the project status changes, instead of relying on spreadsheets and scattered messages for each account. The goal is standardized visibility across all clients at once, even when each one has its quirks.


This type of business faces a specific challenge: every client seems to require a different process, which makes standardizing hard. Without automation, each consultant or account manager ends up creating their own way of organizing deliverables, deadlines, and approvals, and that turns into chaos as the agency grows or someone leaves the team.


Without an automated process, the usual result is missed deadlines, deliverables without formal client approval, and rework when it's time to bill or close the month.


## Common Pain Points in Agencies and Consultancies Without Automation


- Every client has a different tracking spreadsheet
- Deliverable approvals done by email, with no central record
- No visibility into the real workload of each consultant
- Late billing from a lack of an automatic trigger at project close
- Rework building a status report for each client manually


## What Can Be Automated in This Type of Operation


- Onboarding for a new client, with automatic forms and checklists
- Deliverable approval, with authorization by account manager or partner
- Deadline and SLA alerts by project or deliverable
- Automatic task generation from a new project card
- Billing triggered automatically when a project stage closes


## Best Practices for Scaling Automation Across Multiple Clients


- Build a standard process and allow small variations per client
- Centralize all project communication, avoiding scatter across email and WhatsApp
- Define SLA by deliverable type, not just by client
- Measure response time at each step to spot bottlenecks

## Frequently asked questions


**Do small agencies also benefit from automation?** Yes, even with few clients, automation avoids rework; see examples at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can you automate without losing per-client personalization?** Yes, a standard process can have controlled variations per client without turning into chaos.


**Does automation replace the account manager?** No. It organizes tasks and deadlines, but the relationship and the decisions stay with the human team.


**Can you automate client billing?** Yes, by triggering billing automatically when a project stage is completed, a key part of automating client accounts at agencies and consultancies.
